title: Slope and Average Rate of Change

PE1-21.hint: The average rate of change on \([a,b]\) is \(\dfrac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}\). It is the slope of the line through the two points of the graph.
slips: Subtracting in a different order on the top and the bottom.
Stopping at \(f(b) - f(a)\) without dividing by \(b - a\).
Mis-evaluating \(f(4)\) as \(16 - 4\). The second term is \(4x\), so it is \(4\cdot 4\).
PE1-21.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

PE1-22.hint: For a linear function the average rate of change on any interval equals the slope. The units are (output units) per (input unit).
slips: Saying "the cyclist is 12 miles from the start". A rate describes change, not position.
Reporting a position, \(15\) or \(51\), instead of the change in position per hour.
PE1-22.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

PE1-36.hint: The average rate of change on \([a,b]\) is \(\dfrac{g(b) - g(a)}{b - a}\). That fraction is also the slope between the two points.
slips: Giving \(g(4) - g(1) = 1\) without dividing by the change in \(x\).
Saying the value is the slope of the curve at one point. A secant line joins two points.
PE1-36.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

items.stem: Let \(f(x) = x^{2} - 4x\). Find the average rate of change on each interval.

parts.a: \(f(4) = 0\) and \(f(1) = -3\), so the average rate of change is \(\dfrac{0-(-3)}{4-1} = 1\).
\(f(3) = -3\) and \(f(0) = 0\), so the average rate of change is \(\dfrac{-3-0}{3-0} = -1\).

items.stem: A cyclist's position, in miles along a trail, after \(t\) hours is \(p(t) = 12t + 3\).

parts.q: Find the average rate of change over \([1,4]\), including units.
Explain what this rate means in the context of the ride.
parts.a: The cyclist moves at a constant \(12\) miles per hour. Every hour the cyclist's position along the trail increases by \(12\) miles.

items.stem: The graph shows \(g(x) = \sqrt{x}\) and a secant line through \(A(1,1)\) and \(B(4,2)\).

parts.q: Find the average rate of change of \(g\) on \([1,4]\).
Explain what that value tells you about the secant line.
parts.a: It is the slope of the secant line through \(A\) and \(B\): the line rises \(1\) unit for every \(3\) units to the right.

Two points on the curve are marked and labeled: A at (1, 1) and B at (4, 2). A dashed straight line passes through A and B and extends a little past each. A legend names the solid curve g(x) = square root of x and the dashed line Secant through A and B. The x-axis is shown from about -0.5 to 5.2 and the y-axis from -0.5 to 2.6. A table of the labeled points is below the graph.
